exercises.name: Basic Step
instructions: Stand close to the platform, within about a foot of it, facing the long side.
Step up with the lead foot and place the whole foot on the platform.
Step up with the other foot so both feet are on top.
Step down with the lead foot and then the other, letting each heel reach the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the heel hang off the back edge, or stepping down far away from the platform.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the lowest platform height, or march the same pattern on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The four-count basic is the base pattern for every other step move.

exercises.name: V-Step on the Step
instructions: Stand behind the centre of the platform with your feet together.
Step the lead foot up to the far corner on its own side.
Step the other foot up to the opposite corner so your feet are wide on top.
Step the lead foot back down to the centre and bring the other foot down beside it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Landing with only the toes on the platform, or letting the knees drop inward in the wide position.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do the same wide-then-narrow pattern on the floor first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The wide placement brings the outer hips into ordinary stepping.

exercises.name: Over the Top
instructions: Stand side-on to the platform with the near foot beside it.
Step the near foot up onto the middle of the platform.
Bring the other foot up, then step the first foot down on the far side.
Bring the trailing foot down beside it and repeat in the other direction.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping across and landing far from the platform, or twisting the knee of the planted foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step up and return to the same side until the sideways step feels secure.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Travelling across the platform adds lateral work to step training.

exercises.name: Step Knee Lift
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip flexors, core, calves
instructions: Stand close to the platform and step the lead foot up with the whole foot on top.
Lift the other knee to about hip height while standing tall on the platform leg.
Lower that foot back to the floor.
Step the lead foot down, then repeat with the other foot leading.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back to raise the knee, or pushing off hard from the floor instead of standing up through the top leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Replace the knee lift with a light toe tap on the platform.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It adds a single-leg balance moment to each step cycle.

exercises.name: Repeater Knee
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hip flexors, calves, core
instructions: Step the lead foot onto the platform near one corner and keep it there.
Lift the other knee, then tap that foot lightly back on the floor.
Repeat the knee lift three times in a row, keeping your weight over the platform leg.
Step down, then start the next set with the other foot leading.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing off the floor foot between lifts, or letting the platform knee cave inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do a single knee lift each time instead of three.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding one leg on the platform for several counts builds leg endurance.

exercises.name: Aerobic March
instructions: Stand tall with your feet under your hips.
March on the spot with one foot meeting the floor on each beat.
Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your legs.
Vary it by travelling forward, back, or to the side, or by lifting the knees higher.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slumping through the trunk, or stamping heavily instead of placing the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the knees low and march at half tempo.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The march is the low-impact base that most aerobic routines are built on.

source.name: City College of San Francisco, Physical Education (aerobic exercise handout)

exercises.name: V-Step
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Step the lead foot forward and out on a diagonal.
Step the other foot forward and out so your feet are wide.
Step the lead foot back to the start and bring the other foot in beside it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning the pattern into a narrow shuffle, or locking the knees in the wide position.
exercises.beginnerModification: Make the V smaller and slow the tempo.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It adds forward and sideways travel to a simple walking pattern.

exercises.name: Mambo
instructions: Stand with your feet together and knees soft.
Step the lead foot forward and shift your weight onto it.
Shift your weight back onto the rear foot.
Step the lead foot back behind you, shift onto it, then return your weight to the other foot and repeat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Taking steps so long that the trunk tips, or keeping the hips stiff.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take smaller steps and leave the arms at your sides.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The mambo teaches smooth weight transfer between the front and back foot.

exercises.name: Rock-Step Cha-Cha
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Step one foot back and rock your weight onto it.
Transfer your weight forward onto the front foot again.
Take three small quick steps on the spot, then repeat starting with the other foot.
exercises.commonMistakes: Making the three quick steps too large, or losing the beat between the rock and the triple step.
exercises.beginnerModification: Replace the three quick steps with two marches.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Mixing slow and quick steps builds rhythm and light footwork.

exercises.name: Box Step
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Step the lead foot across in front of the other foot.
Step the other foot straight back.
Step the lead foot out to the side, then bring the feet together to finish the square.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the knee of the planted foot on the cross step, or rushing so the square collapses.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk through the four placements slowly without music first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The four-point pattern trains coordination and changes of direction.

exercises.name: Chasse Step
instructions: Stand tall with knees soft.
Step one foot out to the side.
Bring the other foot in to meet it with a quick closing step.
Step the first foot out to the side again, then repeat in the other direction.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the feet, or bouncing high instead of gliding.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do a plain step touch until the three-step rhythm feels comfortable.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A quick three-step travel raises the heart rate without jumping.

exercises.name: Pivot Turn
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Step one foot forward and place your weight on the balls of both feet.
Turn 180 degrees toward the back foot, rotating on the balls of the feet.
Shift your weight onto the new front foot, then repeat to return to the start.
exercises.formCue: Step, turn on the balls of the feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning with the heels planted, which twists the knees, or looking down and losing balance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Swap the turn for a four-count march until you are ready to add it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Turning adds a change of direction and a balance challenge to simple choreography.

exercises.name: Low-Impact Jack
instructions: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Tap one foot out to the side while raising both arms out and overhead.
Bring the foot back in as the arms lower.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating at a steady pace.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears, or leaning away from the tapping foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the arms only to shoulder height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It keeps the pattern of a jumping jack while one foot stays on the floor.

exercises.name: Step Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips.
Step onto one foot and shift your weight over it.
Bend the other knee to bring that heel toward your glute.
Set the foot down wide and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Shift, then curl the heel up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Tipping the chest forward, or swinging the leg instead of bending the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Tap the toe behind you instead of curling the heel up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the back of the legs inside a low-impact side-to-side pattern.

source.name: City College of San Francisco, Physical Education (aerobic exercise handout)

exercises.name: Alternating Knee Lift
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step onto one foot and lift the other knee to about hip height.
Lower that foot and step onto it.
Lift the opposite knee and continue alternating in time.
exercises.formCue: Tall spine, knee to hip height.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the knee rises, or dropping the chest toward the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the knee lower, or tap the toe in front instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Knee lifts raise the heart rate while one foot always stays grounded.

exercises.name: Cross-Step Touch
instructions: Stand with your feet together and knees soft.
Step to the side with one foot.
Cross the other foot in front and touch the toe to the floor.
Step that foot back out to its own side and cross-touch with the first foot.
exercises.commonMistakes: Putting weight on the crossing foot, or twisting the knees instead of turning from the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Touch the foot beside the standing foot instead of crossing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The crossing touch adds hip movement and coordination to a basic side step.

exercises.name: Dance Hip Circles
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, glutes, hip rotators, lower back
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and knees soft.
Push your hips to one side, then to the back, the other side, and the front.
Join the four points into one smooth circle.
Complete several circles, then reverse the direction.
exercises.formCue: Knees soft, circle from the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Locking the knees, or swaying the shoulders instead of moving the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do only the side-to-side shifts before linking the full circle.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Controlled hip circles loosen the hips and trunk for dance work.

exercises.name: Side-to-Side Rock
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than your hips and knees soft.
Shift your weight onto one foot and let the other heel lift.
Shift smoothly across to the other foot.
Keep rocking at a slow, even tempo while letting your breathing settle.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stopping suddenly after hard work instead of slowing down gradually, or locking the knees.
exercises.beginnerModification: Narrow the stance and make the shift smaller.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Simple rhythmic movement brings the heart rate down gradually before stretching.
